adjudication.rationale: Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration reads the legacy site setting value `embeddable_hosts`, splits it into lines, and then executes raw SQL with direct string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`. If any host line contains a single quote (or other SQL-special characters), the SQL becomes invalid and the migration can crash; because it’s unescaped interpolation, it also creates an SQL injection vector in the migration context (the value ultimately originates from an admin-configurable setting stored in DB). A safer approach would be using `quote(h)` / bind params / ActiveRecord insert APIs.
